help.summary: The account's lead metric: utilization of one window and when it resets. Choose the window per account under Accounts.
help.state: What the last poll did: OK, fetching, limit reached (the API rejects requests until the window resets), paused (throttled), error, or token rejected.
help.raw: Every header the API returned, unchanged. Identifying values are masked by default; headers the app does not know yet are marked as new.
help.cost: What one probe costs: the tokens of the tiny request used to read the limits, and the model it was sent to.
help.timeline: One bar per account and window. The bar is the full capacity (100 %), the fill the current utilization. The white line beneath is the time from now (left) to the reset (right) and ends where the window is expected to run out; all the way means it lasts.
help.token: A long-lived token from `claude setup-token`. It is stored encrypted in this browser and only ever sent to the bundled proxy.
help.primaryWindow: The window shown as the big number on the card. 'Most used' picks whichever window is fullest right now.
help.notificationsAccount: Whether threshold notifications fire for this account. Notifications must also be enabled in Settings.
help.color: Used for the card edge and this account's line in the history chart.
help.polling: How often each account is probed and how long snapshots are kept. Each probe costs about 35 tokens of quota.
help.thresholds: Warn and critical levels in percent. They drive the ring glow, the traffic light on the right edge of each card and the browser notifications.
help.notifications: Sends a browser notification when a window crosses a threshold. Fires once per crossing, not on every poll.
help.appearance: Theme and language of the interface.
help.export: Accounts export the encrypted vault file as is. History exports never contain tokens.
help.import: Merge or replace accounts from an exported vault file. You need the passphrase that file was created with.
help.remember: Keeps the vault open for this browser tab. Closing the tab locks it again.
help.forecast: The slope of the utilization is fitted by linear regression over the snapshots of the current cycle and extended to 100 % or to the reset. For the session window the look-back decides how much history enters; week windows always use the whole cycle from 0 %. The thin arc inside each ring is a cycle clock from the last reset to the next, ending where the window is expected to run out.

help_page.title: Getting a token
help_page.intro: Quotlyn reads your limits with a token from the Claude CLI. You need one token per account you want to watch. The token is long-lived and grants inference access to that subscription, so treat it like a password.

items.p: If you do not have it yet, install Claude Code and start it once.

items.h: Sign in with the account you want to watch
items.p: On first start the CLI opens the browser for sign-in. If the CLI is already signed in with a different account, run /logout inside the CLI, then /login, and pick the right account in the browser.
Run the command below in your terminal (not inside the CLI session). It opens the browser again, asks for approval and prints a token that starts with sk-ant-oat01-.
Open Accounts, choose a name and colour, paste the token and press Test token. A green line with the current percentages means everything works.
Sign out of the CLI, sign in with the next account and create its token the same way.

notes.title: Good to know
items: Tokens stay encrypted in this browser and are only sent to the bundled proxy on your machine.
A token cannot read your profile or billing data. Quotlyn only sees the rate-limit headers of a tiny request.
If a card shows Token rejected, the token was revoked or mistyped. Create a new one and replace it under Accounts.
How to revoke a token is described in the Claude Code documentation.
